reproducibility.determinism: verified: identical grades across repeated runs (bench 3/3, armchair 4/4, restaurant chairs 4/4, probe 5/5)
reproducibility.note: NDCG reproducible when rubric_hash pinned. Original SE-20260713 used an earlier unpinned rubric; re-run under pinned 99a0e992a992 reproduces aggregate within +-0.01 (IW 0.944->0.953, SB 0.936->0.935); a minority of borderline queries shifted with rubric evolution. [2026-08-07 correction: IW re-captured via the storefront /?s= engine (shopper-facing), replacing the Store-API capture; both stores graded under pinned rubric 99a0e992a992.]

datasets.name: Synonym / category
datasets.takeaway: Legacy IW returns equivalents fuzzily (accent chair works, with off-type items); the new SB store is strict — misses accent chair, kitchen stool, sofa entirely.

datasets.name: Attribute (material+type)
datasets.takeaway: Broken on both — walnut/marble/velvet return nothing; only leather combinations resolve.

datasets.name: Job-function / intent
datasets.takeaway: Natural-language intent is nearly dead on both — only outdoor seating returns anything, and only on the legacy storefront.

datasets.name: Head terms
datasets.takeaway: dining table works on both; console table misses on both.

datasets.name: Literal (product-name queries)
datasets.takeaway: Product-name (SKU) search is weak — Industry West finds enrique only; Seven Bonde finds piccolo only.

datasets.name: Intent (category-name labels)
datasets.takeaway: The category word Seating returns products on the legacy IW storefront but nothing on the new SB search; promo labels correctly return nothing.

IW.verdict: Broad but fuzzy — answers 40% of queries, but 14% of results are off-target.

SB.verdict: Precise but narrow — clean results (95% on-target), but answers only 26%.

SB.name: Seven Bonde
SB.note: search is in-session Storefront GraphQL; server-side replay not available

findings.title: Attribute search is broken on both stores
findings.detail: walnut/oak dining table, marble coffee/side table, velvet/boucle/cane/woven chair return 0 on both, despite the catalog stocking marble, oak and leather. A shopper who names a material plus a type hits a dead end.

findings.title: Natural-language intent returns nothing on both
findings.detail: furnish a living room, dining set for 6, home office, small space seating, reading chair, restaurant chairs all return 0 on both stores. Only outdoor seating returns anything, and only on the legacy storefront.

findings.title: The migration swaps one flaw for another
findings.detail: The legacy Industry West storefront casts a wide net (40% of queries answered) but is fuzzy — 14% of results are off-target (accent chair returns a side table). The new Seven Bonde store matches strictly (only 5% off-target) but answers just 26%, missing common words like kitchen stool, accent chair and sofa.

findings.title: Product-name (SKU) search is unreliable
findings.detail: Industry West finds enrique but not monica/erik/piccolo; Seven Bonde finds only piccolo. Shoppers searching a known product name often get nothing.

findings.title: STRENGTH: core product-type and leather search works well
findings.detail: bar stool, counter stool, dining chair, lounge chair and leather dining chair return strong, relevant sets on both stores (NDCG ~0.94). Seven Bonde results in particular are clean when present.

findings.title: Recommendations — Not exposed via the WooCommerce Store API (related/upsell products are rendered server-side)
findings.detail: Not exposed via the WooCommerce Store API (related/upsell products are rendered server-side). Needs rendered capture to inspect.

board_meta.engine_note: Industry West evaluated on its live STOREFRONT search (/?s=, the engine shoppers use); Seven Bonde on its in-session predictive search (the AND-of-prefix query its search box builds). Earlier Store-API / loose-query captures measured different engines and were replaced. Seven Bonde is the store Industry West is migrating to.
